chunks.text:
Human Resources Policy > Overview & values > Purpose, applicability, and culture > Governing principles

- The manual is developed along the guidelines of the UAE Labour Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, effective 2 February 2022), as amended.
- In case of inconsistency between the manual and the Labour Law, the legislation takes precedence.
- In case of inconsistency between the manual and an employment contract, the employment contract takes precedence, provided it is not less beneficial than prescribed by law.
- Where a situation is not covered by the manual, the UAE Labour Law is consulted.
- The manual is under the supervision of the CEO; amendments follow the Delegation of Authority, and superseded versions are retained for reference. Queries are registered with the Head of HR.

Human Resources Policy > Overview & values > Purpose, applicability, and culture > Organisation & Emiratisation

- Nebras runs a delayered structure — a CEO at the top with CXOs reporting to the CEO. The structure remains evolutionary and is normally reviewed on a two-year cycle, with changes justified by a business case.
- Corporate-level structural changes (positions reporting to the CEO and all Functional Heads) require Board of Managers approval; changes below Functional Head require CEO approval.
- Nebras supports the UAE’s nationalisation initiatives, designing roles suitable for UAE Nationals with a strategic target workforce composition of 50–60% UAE Nationals.

Key terms used throughout: EOSB (End of Service Benefits), Dependants (immediate family on a Nebras employee’s sponsorship), Point of origin (the employee’s country of origin as stated in their contract), MOH (Ministry of Health), and UAEN (UAE National).

chunks.text:
Human Resources Policy > Recruitment & onboarding > Workforce planning through confirmation of service

In November the CEO issues a workforce-planning format to Managers and Department Heads. Department Heads finalise requirements and draft job descriptions (reviewed and approved by HR); HR consolidates the total requirement, obtains approval, and initiates recruitment.

Internal candidates are considered first. Candidates are sourced through agencies as appropriate (executive search for grades 1–3; Central Bank HR may assist for Nationals). HR screens applications and shortlists via online or in-person interviews.

Shortlisted candidates attend a focused interview with the Department Head or manager to assess function-specific competence. Feedback and the order of choice are returned to HR. Selection panels vary by grade, with senior roles reporting to the CEO cleared by the Board of Managers.

HR prepares the appointment letter for CEO signature. Every appointment is conditional on a satisfactory medical, completion of visa and immigration formalities, proof of resignation from the previous employer, attested educational certificates, and reference/experience letters.

Pre-employment background checks are mandatory and tailored to role and seniority — covering sanctions/PEP/security, criminal records, financial history, and professional references. Results are reviewed by HR, the hiring manager, and (where issues arise) the CEO and relevant Board committee, and recorded in the employee file. Board members are reviewed and approved by CBUAE supervision.

Human Resources Policy > Working hours & attendance > Hours, overtime, remote work, and missions > Standard hours

- Standard working time is 8 hours/day, 4.5 hours on Friday, totalling 36.5 hours/week (Labour Law Art. 17). The eight daily hours may be scheduled between 07:30 and 21:00 depending on the role.
- During the holy month of Ramadan, working hours are reduced by at least two hours, or as instructed by the Federal Government.
- Shift arrangements are prepared by the Direct Supervisor with HR and CEO approval. Work on weekly days off or public holidays requires prior Department Head approval, with HR informed in advance.

chunks.text:
Human Resources Policy > Working hours & attendance > Hours, overtime, remote work, and missions > Overtime

- Overtime is payable to employees in grades 7–8, subject to: more than half an hour worked per day; not exceeding 11.5 hours/week; calculated at basic salary on a pro-rata basis; and capped at AED 2,000/month.
- Total working hours including overtime MUST NOT exceed 144 hours over any 3-week period — a maximum of 11.5 overtime hours in a week. The statutory overtime cap is 2 hours/day (Art. 19), paid at basic + 25% (daytime) or basic + 50%, or a compensatory rest day, for night/holiday work.

- Employees submit tentative annual-leave dates at the start of the year for consolidation into an annual leave plan ensuring fairness and adequate coverage.
- Unused annual leave may be carried forward by no more than 8 days; leave is not cashed during employment, only at end of service (exceptional further accumulation needs Management approval).

- Sick leave taken during annual leave counts as annual leave; if illness extends beyond it, sick leave begins on the scheduled return date subject to a satisfactory medical report.

Human Resources Policy > Compensation & benefits > Pay, allowances, and benefits > Benefits

- Health insurance — covers self and dependants (spouse and 3 children up to age 18 or visa validity); grades 1–2 in category A, grades 3–8 in category B. Double insurance is not permitted; UAE Nationals receive a Thiqa Top-Up plan.
- Group life & personal accident — all employees are covered (no dependants enrolled).
- Pension — UAE Nationals are enrolled with GPSSA: employer contributes 15% and the employee 5% of pensionable salary; GCC Nationals follow their home-country scheme.
- Education allowance — per child per annum for up to 3 children aged 3–18 (no cap for UAE Nationals): grade 1 — AED 65,000; grades 2–4 — AED 50,000; grades 5–6 — AED 40,000; grades 7–8 — AED 30,000.
- Housing loan — grades 1–2 are eligible for an interest-free loan up to AED 120,000 per 6 months, repaid over 6 months; fully repayable on resignation.
- Annual leave airfare — IATA rate for employee, spouse, and up to 3 children under 18 with valid UAE residency; business class for grades 1–2, economy for grades 3–8.
- Relocation — international joiners receive one-way passage and hotel accommodation up to 30 nights; grades 1–3 receive a relocation allowance of one Basic Allowance up to AED 25,000.

chunks.text:
Human Resources Policy > Conduct & ethics > Professional ethics and code of conduct > Integrity obligations

- Conflicts of interest MUST be disclosed and approved in writing by the Board/CEO. Staff disclose annually; Board members on joining or renewal. Accepted disclosures are stored confidentially by HR for 5 years.
- Gifts & bribes — commissions, kickbacks, and undesirable gifts MUST NOT be accepted. A gift worth more than AED 250 must be disclosed in writing to the CEO for permission; the Anti-Bribery & Corruption policy further limits gifts/hospitality to AED 500, all declared and logged in an official register.
- Outside activities — employees MUST NOT be gainfully engaged with another employer during or outside office hours (volunteering and charity are exempt). No preferential treatment or personal borrowing/lending between employees.
- Anti-money laundering — employees familiarise themselves with relevant federal laws and report suspicious activity to the concerned authorities.
- Confidentiality — customer and proprietary information MUST NOT be shared with unauthorised third parties; individual salaries and bonuses are not discussed; documents are stored securely and shredded when unwanted.

- Beyond the acts listed under Labour Law No. 33 of 2021, misconduct includes unauthorised absence, insubordination, failure to follow instructions, disregarding safety, fighting, illegal activity, indecent or coercive conduct, discourtesy, and divulging confidential information.

Human Resources Policy > Grievance & disciplinary > Raising concerns and corrective action > Grievance procedure

- Covers perceived unfair treatment, working conditions, interpersonal conflicts, and matters under Article 111 of the Labour Law — but cannot be used to appeal a disciplinary action already initiated (a separate appeals process applies).

chunks.text:
Human Resources Policy > Grievance & disciplinary > Raising concerns and corrective action > Disciplinary process

On becoming aware of misconduct, the immediate supervisor investigates, discusses the incident with the employee, gives them the opportunity to explain, and records the discussion and any commitment to improve.

More serious matters are reported to the Department Head in writing (findings, employee responses, recommendation). The Department Head meets the employee and supervisor within 3 days and may involve HR.

For employees below Manager, HR constitutes a 3-member investigation committee; for Manager and above, the committee is constituted by the CEO and works under the CEO’s guidance.

Actions escalate through verbal warning, first written warning, final written warning, to termination. Discontinuation of a Manager’s service requires approval from the relevant Board committee; other terminations require CEO approval.

Disciplinary letters are signed by the Department Head/CEO and documented in the employee record. The procedure is concluded within 30 days of occurrence or reporting to HR.

No disciplinary action is taken without a proper enquiry recorded in writing, and employees MUST be given a fair chance to defend themselves. The committee may recommend suspension pending inquiry (without pay where a crime is alleged). No employee under inquiry may resign until it concludes. An employee proved innocent is reinstated with salary for the suspension period.

Human Resources Policy > End of service > Resignation, termination, and benefits > End-of-service payments

- Settlement includes salary to the last working day, payment in lieu of accrued annual leave, pro-rata annual air passage (if 6+ months completed since the last entitlement), and notice-period salary where applicable.
- Repatriation: a one-way ticket home for self and dependants once the visa is cancelled; grades 1–3 receive a repatriation allowance up to AED 5,000. Not payable if transferring to another UAE role.

Human Resources Policy > Whistleblowing & disclosure > Speaking up, disclosures, and behaviours > Whistleblowing

- Reportable concerns include unethical conduct, fraud, conflicts of interest, confidentiality breaches, theft, bribery, money laundering, misrepresentation of financials, discrimination or harassment, health & safety hazards, and suspected modern slavery or human trafficking.
- Concerns are submitted in writing, signed, in a sealed envelope marked “Highly Confidential – WB” to the designated Board member/CEO. The sender MUST NOT write their name on the outside; anonymous letters are not actioned.

- Whistleblowers are protected from retaliation and their anonymity preserved where possible; false or malicious whistleblowing attracts disciplinary action. A whistleblower may be rewarded where the company avoids reputational or financial loss.
